title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 241 (Application to Tribunal for relief in cases of oppression and mismanagement)

content.overview: Section 241 lets eligible members apply to the Tribunal where the company's affairs are conducted in a manner prejudicial to the public interest or oppressive to members, or where a material change is likely to cause that result.
content.glance: Section 241 lets eligible members apply to the Tribunal where the company's affairs are conducted in a manner prejudicial to the public interest or oppressive to members, or where a material change is likely to cause that result.
content.study: An application under section 241 is made by members who meet the section 244 threshold, subject to the Tribunal's waiver power. The complaint is that the company's affairs are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to the public interest or oppressive to any member, or that a material change in management or control is likely to lead to that result. A mere loss of confidence is not enough. Relief is granted under section 242; just and equitable winding up is a separate ground under section 271.

sections.heading: Who may apply
sections.body: Members who satisfy the section 244 numerical or shareholding threshold may apply, and the Tribunal may waive the threshold.

sections.heading: Grounds
sections.body: Prejudicial conduct, oppression of members, or a material change likely to produce that result.

sections.heading: Limit
sections.body: Loss of confidence alone does not make out oppression or mismanagement.
